# walk paths


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A learner often wants to learn more than one concept. “I want to learn
how LLMs work” needs tokenizers, embeddings, attention, transformers and
more, in a given order. A walk keeps that goal and that order on the
learning shelf.

The planner (one model call) proposes the steps. It uses the concepts on
the shelf when they fit. It makes new concepts for the topics that the
shelf does not have. Then the learner can change the path: move, skip,
mark as known, add and split steps.

A walk keeps the outcome of each check on its step, and
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state)
counts them. A concept that the learner learns anywhere is known in each
walk that has it. An old walk with no `mode` (a path, from before
0.0.16) becomes a topic walk once, in the background at the start of the
app, with its progress
([`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_path)).

Import the modules that this notebook uses.

## The document

A walk is one vault document of kind `journey`. Its meta has the goal, a
title, a subject, and the steps. Each step has a slug, a status (`todo`,
`known` or `skip`) and the reason that it is in the path.

## Change the steps

`journey_step` makes one change to one step: up, down, skip, known, todo
or remove. `journey_add` adds a step at the end, or before another step.
A step of a walk gets a short check.

### The source map

A goal can name its sources, such as `course22p2` and `fastbook`. The
Start box files them as chips.
[`chip_docs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#chip_docs)
gives the documents of each chip that is in the vault: a folder, a repo,
a GitHub repo or one vault document.
[`source_map`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#source_map)
gives the planner, for each chip, its root and up to 40 documents, each
as its short title and its first heading. So the plan can name the
document of each step.

[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan) saves
the walk. A step can name a known slug, or a known name or alias. Then
it uses that concept and keeps its state. Each other step becomes a new
concept, with the steps it needs as its prereqs. With `sources`,
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan) links
each new concept to the passages that name it in the learner’s own
sources. With a source map, each step also keeps the `doc` it comes from
(only a title from the map), `hands='notebook'` for a step that builds
part of the goal, what that notebook `makes`, and the `data` entries
that it names. A step keeps only the fields that have a value.

## Walks

A walk from a source has `mode='walk'`. It is the reading path: one step
for each idea, in reading order. Each step has the passage to read
(`read`) and the check to do (`check`).

[`_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/edit.html#_check) picks
the check of one concept. It uses the stats and the profile of the
learner, as
[`Tutor.ask_on`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor.ask_on)
does. abhyasa runs no code: when the chosen way is code, the check kind
is `notebook`, and the step runs in Leela. On a tool walk (`tool=True`),
or for a step that needs a library, its reason says so. A step that the
plan marks `hands='notebook'` gets it too.

[`short_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#short_check)
gives a short-answer check in a text way. A walk uses it when a demo or
an order check has no card. The way comes from the text ways of the
concept, or from all text ways. A code way is not in the list, because
its check is a code task.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

### A walk has a most number of steps

A long source, such as a docs site, can have 60 ideas or more. A walk of
that length is too long to finish, and each step costs model calls for
its note and its check. So a walk has at most `val('walks.steps')` steps
(12 by default; you can change it on the Settings page). When a source
has more ideas,
[`main_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#main_steps)
asks the model one time to pick the main ideas, with the prompt
`walk.pick`. You can change it on the Settings page. When the reply has
fewer valid numbers, the first ideas that are not picked fill the walk
in source order. The steps keep the order of the source, and a
prerequisite that is picked comes before the idea that needs it. The
pick happens when the walk is made, before any step writes a note or a
check. The other ideas stay on the shelf as concepts. The walk keeps
their slugs in `more`, so the plan can say how many more ideas the
source has.

A demo, an order check or a code task takes longer than a short answer.
So at most a share of the steps of a walk get one (the setting
`walks.hands`, a third by default, rounded down, and at least 1 in a
walk of 3 steps or more).
[`cap_hands`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#cap_hands)
counts the hands-on checks in walk order, after
[`main_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#main_steps).
When the walk has its share, each later step gets a check in its text
ways. The count does not depend on chance, so a test can check it. A
step that the plan marks `hands='notebook'` builds part of the goal, so
[`cap_hands`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#cap_hands)
leaves it as it is.
[`hands_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#hands_count)
counts it apart. The share only warns: the walk editor shows the counts,
and nothing stops a walk with more.

[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_from_topic)
plans a path to the goal. With the chips of the Start box, the planner
sees the source map and the data list, and each step reads the paragraph
of its `doc` that names the most main words of the idea, and at least
half of them. A step with no `doc` reads the first passage in your
sources that names the idea or an alias. A passage from a source that
the goal named may instead name every main word of the idea. A weak
match is no source: the step has no `read`, the page shows the tutor’s
words, and research can look on the web.

### Your data

A course or a walk can keep folders of your own data in `data`, as a
list of `{path, note}`. abhyasa does not file these folders and does not
learn from them. The exercises run on them in Leela.
[`data_row`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#data_row)
checks one folder, and
[`keep_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#keep_data)
adds it to a list.
[`data_entries`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#data_entries)
makes the data entries of a notebook spec: an upper-case name from the
folder name, the path, and `what`, with the note and a short listing of
the folder.
[`with_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#with_data)
adds them to the entries of a step.

### data_row

``` python
def data_row(
    path, note:str=''
)->dict:
```

*The data folder `path` as a row `{path, note}`, with `~` for the home
folder. A `ValueError` says in one line why abhyasa cannot use it.*

A folder in your home folder is a data row, with `~` and its note. A
path outside the home folder, a path that is not a folder, and a ninth
folder are refused, each with one plain line. Here the home folder is a
temporary folder.

``` python
home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (eps := home/'ramayana-episodes').mkdir(); (eps/'episodes.json').write_text('{}'); (eps/'characters.json').write_text('[]'); (eps/'.hidden').write_text('')
    rows = keep_data([], str(eps), 'The 418 episodes:\nmy scenarios run on them.')
    test_eq(rows, [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them.')])
    test_eq(keep_data(rows, '~/ramayana-episodes', 'New note.'), [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='New note.')])   # one row for each path
    for bad, said in (('/etc', 'not in your home folder'), (str(eps/'episodes.json'), 'no folder'), ('~/nothing', 'no folder')):
        with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, said): keep_data(rows, bad)
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'at most 8'): keep_data([dict(path=f'~/d{k}', note='') for k in range(8)], str(eps))
    es = data_entries(rows)
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
test_eq(es, [dict(name='RAMAYANA_EPISODES', path='~/ramayana-episodes', what='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them. It holds: characters.json, episodes.json.', need=False)])
```

A name that a step uses already gets a number.
[`with_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#with_data)
keeps the entries of the step first, and adds only the folders that they
do not have. Each entry passes the check of a notebook spec.

``` python
from abhyasa.contract import validate_nb_spec, _GOOD
```

``` python
test_eq([e['name'] for e in data_entries([dict(path='~/x/2024 data', note=''), dict(path='~/y/2024-data', note='')], taken=['D_2024_DATA'])], ['D_2024_DATA_2', 'D_2024_DATA_3'])
step = [dict(name='IMAGES', path='~/Pictures/comic', what='your images', need=True)]
test_eq([e['name'] for e in with_data(step, [dict(path='~/Pictures/comic', note=''), dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='')])], ['IMAGES', 'RAMAYANA_EPISODES'])
test_eq(with_data(step, None), step)
test_eq(validate_nb_spec({**_GOOD, 'data': es})['data'], es)
```

## Change a step, read the rail

`walk_step` merges changes into one step and saves the walk.
`merge_journey` merges changes into the fields of the walk, such as
`sitting`. Both hold one lock for each walk id, so two requests on one
walk do not lose a change.
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state)
gives each step a dot for the rail: `done` (outcome `solid`), `shaky`
(outcome `fragile`, `gap` or `misconception`), `skipped`, `known`, `now`
(the first step with no outcome and the status `todo`) or `todo`.

The sections of a walk from a paper or a link follow the document: a new
document or a new section name starts a section. A walk from a topic or
a goal has no source document (`source` is empty). Its sections are the
sections of the plan (the `section` of a step), so a passage from
another document does not start a section, and “Section done” shows only
at the end of a plan section.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L569"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


`walk_slug` finds the step by its concept. A step that moved still gets
the change, and a step that left the walk gets nothing.

``` python
ws = temp_learning(); ws.put_journey(dict(id='wsl', title='W', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b')]))
test_eq(ws.walk_slug('wsl', 'b', note='N').steps[1]['note'], 'N'); test_is(ws.walk_slug('wsl', 'zz', note='N'), None)
```

With `by`,
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state)
reads the concepts too. An idea that you learned in a session or in
another walk is `known (learned elsewhere)`: it counts as done, and the
current step is the next idea that you do not know.

``` python
kn = temp_learning(); kn.put('A', 'a', 'ml'); kn.put('B', 'b', 'ml'); kn.update('a', floor=4, seen=1)
kj = dict(id='k', source=None, steps=[dict(slug='a', status='todo'), dict(slug='b', status='todo')])
test_eq(walk_state(kj).current, 0)   # with no concepts, step a is still to do
ks = walk_state(kj, {c.slug: c for c in kn.concepts()})
test_eq([s.dot for s in ks.steps], ['known', 'now']); test_eq((ks.current, ks.done, ks.steps[0].elsewhere), (1, 1, True))
```

time of its check.

## Rabbit holes

A step can need an idea that you have not learned. For example, the
scaling by √dk in a paper on attention needs gradients. These functions
find what is missing, make a short side walk on it, and link the side
walk back to the step.

[`needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#needs)
lists the prereqs of a concept, then its gaps. A need is met at depth
`READY` (3) or more, as in `model.ready`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L591"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### needs

``` python
def needs(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The prereqs, then the gaps, of concept `slug` that are on the shelf.
`ok` is true at depth `READY` or more.*

[`pick_way_down`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#pick_way_down)
picks how to learn a missing idea:

- `primer`: one step and one short check. You met the idea before (depth
  1 or 2), or it needs no other idea that you have not learned.
- `walk`: a side walk on the chain, at most `walks.chain` (4 by default)
  ideas. The chain is the unready prereqs, deepest first, then the idea.
- `session`: a longer chain. It opens as its own walk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L608"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### pick_way_down

``` python
def pick_way_down(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*How to learn concept `slug` before you go on: a `primer`, a side `walk`
or its own `session`, with why in one line.*

[`detour`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#detour)
makes the side walk and starts it. It keeps `parent` (the walk and the
step that opened it) and `depth`. A side walk of a side walk has depth
2. Past `walks.depth` (2 by default), only its own session can open, at
depth 0. With no chain on the shelf, the side walk is a short path that
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan) makes,
with steps as
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_from_topic)
makes them. The planned walk is not kept. It always ends on the idea.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L631"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make and start a side walk on concept `slug`, as a child of `parent`
(`{walk, step}`, or a place in Leela).*

[`parent_step`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#parent_step)
gives the walk and the step that opened side walk `j`, when both are
still there. Else it gives `(None, None)`. The walk page, the side pane,
the history and the walk list use it, so they agree on “the parent step
is still there”. With `js`, a dictionary of walks by id, it reads no
walk from the shelf.

[`trail`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#trail)
gives the walks from the root walk down to a side walk, for the crumbs.
[`back_from`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#back_from)
keeps the result of a side walk on the step that opened it, in
`detours`. The result is the outcome of the last step, or `skipped`. One
side walk has one record. When you come back again with a new outcome,
the record changes, and `at` is the time of the new outcome. A later
skip does not change a record.

[`for_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#for_talk)
tells a walk that is for the room: a side walk that a talk opened (its
parent is `{talk, slide}`), or the walk that a talk was made from, from
a path, a walk with no source (its parent is `{journey, for: 'talk'}`).
Such a walk is not your own learning, so the pages that list your walks
and the steps you read skip it.

### for_talk

``` python
def for_talk(
    j
)->bool:
```

*Whether walk `j` is for a talk: a side walk that a talk opened beside a
slide, or the walk that a talk was made from, from a path.*

A walk with a talk parent, or one made for a talk from a path, is for
the room. A walk with a walk parent, or with no parent, is your own.

``` python
assert for_talk(dict(parent={'talk': 't-1', 'slide': 's3'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'walk': 'w-1', 'step': 0}))
assert for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1', 'for': 'talk'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1'}))
assert not for_talk({}) and not for_talk(None) and not for_talk(dict(parent=None))
```

### The place that you used last

[`last_place`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#last_place)
says where Continue goes. It is the one function for the top bar, the
card on Today and the card of a course. A place is a step of a walk that
is not finished, or an open session with no walk. Each walk gives the
time that you used it last: the idea that you were on (`here`, which the
idea page writes), the newest idea that you read, or the start. A
session gives the time of its last change. The newest place wins. A side
walk counts as the step that opened it, so Continue goes back to the
paper. Only the newest `most` walks are read. The step is the idea that
you were on when it is not done, else the current step of the walk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L706"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def last_place(

)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*The place that you used last, or None. A walk place has `walk`, `step`,
`title`, `done`, `total` and `course`; a session place has* `session`
and `title`. Each has `at`, the time that you used it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L702"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


### is_open

``` python
def is_open(
    s
)->bool:
```

*Whether filed session `s` is open: it has a log, it did not end, and it
has an answer or an open question.*

A walk that you read now wins over an older open session, and the
session wins when you use it after the walk.

``` python
pl2 = temp_learning(); pl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); pl2.put('Fusion', 'Join two lists.', 'ml')
two = [dict(slug='ranking', status='todo', check={}), dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})]
now = time.time()
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='wa', title='Walk A', mode='walk', steps=two, started=now - 60, here=dict(step=1, at=now - 30)))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 600, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
p = last_place(pl2)
test_eq((p.walk, p.step, p.title, p.done, p.total), ('wa', 1, 'Walk A', 0, 2))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
test_eq((last_place(pl2).session, last_place(pl2).title), ('s1', 'Ranking'))
```

A side walk counts as the step that opened it. A finished walk, a walk
for a talk and an ended session are not places.

``` python
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 900, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], ended=now - 900)
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='side', title='Side', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})], parent=dict(walk='wa', step=1, slug='fusion'), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
test_eq((last_place(pl2).walk, last_place(pl2).step), ('wa', 1))
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='talk', title='Talk', mode='walk', steps=two, parent=dict(talk='t1', slide='s1'), here=dict(step=0, at=now + 9)))
test_eq(last_place(pl2).walk, 'wa')
for x in ('wa', 'side'): pl2.merge_journey(x, steps=[{**s, 'done': dict(outcome='solid', at=now)} for s in pl2.journey(x).steps])
test_eq(last_place(pl2), None)
```

### An old path becomes a walk

Before 0.0.16 a goal could give a path: a walk with no `mode`, no
passage and no check of its own.
[`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_path)
makes such a path a topic walk, one time, with the same id: the same
steps in the same order, each with a check, as
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_from_topic)
does. A step that you marked known or skipped stays so, and an idea that
you learned is known.

The walk keeps the progress of the sessions of the path. A step with
answers is done or shaky. The newest open session is the sitting, with
its open question, which goes on the shelf of open questions
([`_keep_open`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#_keep_open)),
so the step shows it. `started` and `here` come from the sessions, so an
old path does not become the newest walk.

[`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_path)
does not search the sources, so it is fast.
[`step_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#step_read)
finds the passage of one step when its idea opens.
[`walk_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_paths)
does it for each path, and gives the ids.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L769"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

[`add_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#add_topic)
adds a topic by name. When the shelf knows the name,
[`add_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#add_topic)
uses that concept. For a new name, the model writes a short statement.

``` python

    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, j, name:str, sources:NoneType=None

```

*The slug of the concept `name` on the shelf. The tutor writes a new
concept when the shelf has none: the name goes in a fence, with no
control marks, cut to `NAME_MOST`. None for a name that is not an idea.*

[`name_gaps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#name_gaps)
keeps each idea that you say you do not know as a gap of the concept you
learn. It finds the idea on the shelf by name or alias. Or it adds the
idea with a short statement. Next time the gap comes first, but it does
not block the concept.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L817"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### name_gaps

``` python
def name_gaps(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, slug:str, terms, sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Find or add a concept for each idea in `terms`, and keep it as a gap of
`slug`. Return the gap slugs.*

A new idea becomes a concept with a statement and the gap provenance.
[`name_gaps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#name_gaps)
finds an idea that is already on the shelf by its alias. It does not add
that idea again.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
ngl = temp_learning(); ngl.put('Functions and the neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml'); ngl.put('Bias', 'A constant added to z.', 'ml', aliases=['the bias'])
gask = Fake({'The idea: the loop': dict(name='Weighted sum as a loop', statement='A loop adds each weight times its input.')})
test_eq(name_gaps(ngl, gask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['the loop', 'the bias', 'the loop']), ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop', 'bias'])
g = ngl.concept('weighted-sum-as-a-loop')
test_eq((g.aliases, g.provenance[0]['src'], g.provenance[0]['of']), (['the loop'], 'gap', 'functions-and-the-neuron'))
test_eq(ngl.concept('functions-and-the-neuron').gaps, ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop', 'bias'])
```

A term such as `x` makes no concept, and the tutor is not asked about
it.

``` python
n0 = len(gask.calls)
test_eq(name_gaps(ngl, gask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['x', ' ']), [])
test_eq((len(gask.calls), ngl.concept('x')), (n0, None))
```

[`split`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#split)
divides a big step into smaller steps. It runs
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
over the statement of the step and the passages from the learner’s
sources. The concepts that it finds go before the step, as its prereqs.

### Learning.repair_subjects

``` python
def repair_subjects()->list:
```

*One time on a vault: give the subject of its walk to each concept of
the walk that has none (a walk with no subject uses the most common one
of its concepts). The group stays. A concept that you moved by hand
stays. Return the slugs that changed.*

### A concept with no subject gets the subject of its walk

[`split`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#split)
gives its parts the subject of the step, or else the subject of the
walk.
[`_fill_subject`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#_fill_subject)
gives the subject of a walk to the concepts that it made with none. A
concept that you moved by hand stays.

``` python
sp = temp_learning(); sp.put('Attention', 'Weights on values.')                       # no subject
sp.put_journey(dict(id='jx', title='T', goal='g', subject='nlp', steps=[dict(slug='attention')], mode='walk', created=0))
spf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Query', statement='A vector.')])})
test_eq(split(sp, spf, 'jx', 'attention'), ['query'])
test_eq(sp.concept('query').subject, 'nlp')                                                # the subject of the walk, as the step has none
```

``` python
sp.put('Key', 'A vector.'); sp.put('Pinned', 'Mine.'); sp.set_group('pinned', ['mine'], by='hand')
test_eq(_fill_subject(sp, ['key', 'pinned', 'query'], 'nlp'), 'nlp')
test_eq([sp.concept(s).subject for s in ('key', 'pinned', 'query')], ['nlp', '', 'nlp'])
sp.put('Value', 'A vector.', 'ml')
test_eq(_fill_subject(sp, ['value', 'attention'], ''), 'ml')                              # the most common subject of the walk
test_eq(sp.concept('attention').subject, 'ml')
```

### One repair for old concepts in General

`repair_subjects` runs one time on a vault. A concept with no subject,
in a walk that has a subject, gets that subject. A walk with no subject
uses the most common subject of its concepts. The group of a concept
stays. A concept that you placed by hand does not move, and the mark
says that the repair ran.

``` python
rs = temp_learning()
for n in ('Alpha one', 'Beta one', 'Gamma one', 'Pinned one', 'Lone one'): rs.put(n, 'Idea.')
rs.put('Delta one', 'Idea.', 'ml'); rs.put('Eps one', 'Idea.')
rs.set_group('beta-one', ['Bits'], by='model'); rs.set_group('pinned-one', ['Mine'], by='hand')
rs.put_journey(dict(id='j1', title='T1', goal='g', subject='transformers', mode='walk', created=0, more=['gamma-one'],
                    steps=[dict(slug=s) for s in ('alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'pinned-one')]))
rs.put_journey(dict(id='j2', title='T2', goal='g', subject='', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='delta-one'), dict(slug='eps-one')]))
rs.v.forget(first(rs.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/subjects']))['id'])
test_eq(sorted(rs.repair_subjects()), ['alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'eps-one', 'gamma-one'])
test_eq([rs.concept(s).subject for s in ('alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'gamma-one', 'pinned-one', 'lone-one', 'eps-one')], ['transformers', 'transformers', 'transformers', '', '', 'ml'])
test_eq((rs.concept('beta-one').group, rs.concept('alpha-one').get('group'), rs.concept('pinned-one').group), (['Bits'], None, ['Mine']))
test_eq(rs.repair_subjects(), [])                                                         # one time
```

``` python
rs.put('Zeta one', 'Idea.'); rs.put_journey(dict(id='j3', title='T3', goal='g', subject='nlp', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='zeta-one')]))
test_eq(rs.repair_subjects(), [])                                                         # the mark is set: it does not look again
test_eq(rs.concept('zeta-one').subject, '')
```

A concept that you kept out of the groups by hand (an empty group) is
not moved by the repair, with or without a group name.

``` python
hs = temp_learning(); hs.put('Kept one', 'Idea.'); hs.set_group('kept-one', [], by='hand')
hs.put_journey(dict(id='j9', title='T9', goal='g', subject='nlp', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='kept-one')]))
hs.v.forget(first(hs.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/subjects']))['id'])
test_eq((hs.repair_subjects(), hs.concept('kept-one').subject, hs.concept('kept-one').group_by), ([], '', 'hand'))
```

## Related topics

[`related`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#related)
gives the concepts next to `slug` in the graph. First come the concepts
that build on it, then the related ones, then its prereqs. The concepts
that are not learned come first.
[`with_step`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#with_step)
finds the walks that have a concept.
[`beyond`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#beyond)
gives what comes after a walk: the concepts that build on its steps and
are not in it.


it.*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


``` python
def related(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, k:int=6, goal:int=None, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Up to `k` concepts next to `slug`: what builds on it, what relates to
it, then what it needs.*

## Tests

A fake model plans a path to LLMs. The shelf has `attention` already, at
depth 3.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
lr.update('attention', floor=3, seen=1)
fake = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='How LLMs work', subject='ml', steps=[
    dict(name='Tokenizers', statement='A tokenizer cuts text into tokens.', slug='', why='The model reads tokens.', needs=[]),
    dict(name='Embeddings', statement='An embedding maps a token to a vector.', slug='', why='Tokens become vectors.', needs=['Tokenizers']),
    dict(name='Attention', statement='', slug='attention', why='The core of a transformer.', needs=['Embeddings']),
    dict(name='Mamba', statement='Mamba is a selective state-space model.', slug='', why='Another way to mix tokens.', needs=['Attention'])])})
j = plan(lr, fake, 'I want to learn how LLMs work', who='Background: codes in Python')
```

[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan) keeps
the order, uses the known concept, and makes the new ones with their
prereqs.

``` python
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in j.steps], ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention', 'mamba'])
test_eq((lr.concept('embeddings').prereqs, lr.concept('mamba').prereqs, lr.concept('mamba').subject), (['tokenizers'], ['attention'], 'ml'))
test_eq(lr.concept('attention').floor, 3)    # a known concept keeps its state
assert 'codes in Python' in fake.calls[-1][0] and 'attention: Attention (depth 3)' in fake.calls[-1][0]
```

A step that is not a
[`real_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/store.html#real_idea),
such as `x` with the statement `x`, is not an idea:
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan) leaves
it out, and makes no concept for it.

``` python
fx = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='T', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='x', statement='x', slug='', why='', needs=[]),
                                                                            dict(name='Tokenizers', statement='', slug='', why='', needs=[])])})
px = plan(lr, fx, 'learn about x')
test_eq(([s['slug'] for s in px.steps], lr.concept('x')), (['tokenizers'], None))
lr.drop_journey(px.id)
```

[`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_path)
makes the path a walk with the same id. Each step has a check. The known
concept is known, and the path is not started: it had no session. A
second call changes nothing.

``` python
w = walk_path(lr, j)
test_eq((w.id, w.mode, w.started, [s['slug'] for s in w.steps]), (j.id, 'walk', None, ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention', 'mamba']))
assert all(s['check'] for s in w.steps)
test_eq(walk_path(lr, w).updated, w.updated)
test_eq(walk_paths(lr), [])
```

A step that the learner learns anywhere is known in the walk too. A step
that is marked known or skipped is done. Then
[`current`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#current)
moves to the next idea.

``` python
lr.update('tokenizers', floor=4, seen=2)
lr.journey_step(j.id, 'embeddings', 'known')
test_eq([s.dot for s in walk_state(lr.journey(j.id), {c.slug: c for c in lr.concepts()}).steps][:2], ['known', 'known'])
test_eq((current(lr, lr.journey(j.id)), current(lr, lr.journey(j.id), skip={'attention'})), ('attention', 'mamba'))
```

A path with sessions keeps its progress when it becomes a walk. The path
below has three steps and two sessions. The first session ended: its
last answer on `embeddings` passed. The second session is open: it has a
fragile answer on `mamba` and an open question on `softmax`.

``` python
lr.put('Softmax', 'Softmax makes weights from scores.', 'ml')
row = lambda slug, o, at: dict(concept=slug, outcome=o, correct=o != 'gap', at=at)
pp = lr.put_journey(dict(id='old-path', title='Old', goal='g', created=50., steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo') for s in ('embeddings', 'mamba', 'softmax')]))
lr.log_session('s8', 'first', journey='old-path', start=1000., updated=1100., ended=1100., log=[row('embeddings', 'gap', 1050.), row('embeddings', 'solid', 1090.)])
lr.log_session('s9', 'second', journey='old-path', start=2000., updated=2100., log=[row('mamba', 'fragile', 2050.)], open=dict(id='q9', concept='softmax'))
w = walk_path(lr, pp)
```

Each step with answers has the outcome of its last answer, and the step
of the open question keeps it. The counts are those of
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state).

``` python
st = walk_state(w)
test_eq([s.dot for s in st.steps], ['done', 'shaky', 'now'])
test_eq((st.done, st.total, w.steps[2]['qid']), (1, 3, 'q9'))
```

The open session is the sitting. `started` is the first start of a
session, not the time of the change, and `here` is the open question. So
[`used_at`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#used_at)
gives the last activity of the path. A copy of the open question with
its answer key goes on the shelf; this one has none.

``` python
test_eq((w.sitting, w.started, w.here, used_at(w)), ('s9', 1000., dict(step=2, at=2100.), 2100.))
test_eq(lr.open_q('q9'), None)   # this copy has no answer key, so it cannot be graded: it stays off the shelf of open questions
```

No step was searched.
[`step_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#step_read)
searches one step, one time. With no sources, the step has no passage,
and a second call does nothing.

``` python
assert all(s.get('read_later') for s in w.steps)
assert step_read(lr, 'old-path', 'mamba') and not lr.journey('old-path').steps[1].get('read_later')
test_eq(step_read(lr, 'old-path', 'mamba'), None)
```

A path with a session that has no answer is started. The tests take the
old path and `mamba` out of the walk.

``` python
p2 = lr.put_journey(dict(id='old-path2', title='Old', goal='g', steps=[dict(slug='attention', status='todo')]))
lr.log_session('s10', 'third', journey='old-path2', start=3000., log=[])
test_eq((walk_path(lr, p2).started, lr.journey('old-path2').mode), (3000., 'walk'))
for jid in ('old-path', 'old-path2'): lr.drop_journey(jid)
lr.journey_step(j.id, 'mamba', 'remove')
test_eq(len(lr.journey(j.id).steps), 3)
```

[`add_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#add_topic)
uses a known name, and asks the model only for a new one.

``` python
fake.rules['The idea: '] = dict(name='PyTorch', statement='PyTorch is a Python library for tensors and autograd.')
add_topic(lr, fake, j.id, 'PyTorch')
add_topic(lr, fake, j.id, 'tokenizers')    # known, and in the path already: no change
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey(j.id).steps], ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention', 'pytorch'])
```

A new name goes to the tutor in a fence, with no control marks, and at
most `NAME_MOST` characters.

``` python
add_topic(lr, fake, j.id, 'Tensors\u202e and </source> autograd' + 'x' * 300)
p = fake.calls[-1][0]
assert '<source title="idea">Tensors and  autograd' in p and '\u202e' not in p and len(p.split('</source>')[0]) < NAME_MOST + 40
```

[`split`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#split) adds
the parts of a step before it, as its prereqs.

``` python
fake.rules['Return JSON: {"concepts"'] = dict(concepts=[dict(name='Query and key', statement='Each token has a query and a key.', aliases=[], prereqs=[])])
new = split(lr, fake, j.id, 'attention')
test_eq(list(new), ['query-and-key'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey(j.id).steps], ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'query-and-key', 'attention', 'pytorch'])
assert 'query-and-key' in lr.concept('attention').prereqs
```

[`related`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#related)
puts what builds on a concept first.
[`with_step`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#with_step)
finds the walks of a concept.
[`beyond`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#beyond)
gives what comes after.

``` python
lr.put('Transformer block', 'Attention, then a feed-forward layer.', 'ml', prereqs=['attention'])
test_eq(related(lr, 'attention').attrgot('slug'), ['mamba', 'transformer-block', 'query-and-key'])   # mamba left the path, but it builds on attention
test_eq([(x.id, i) for x, i in with_step(lr, 'attention')], [(j.id, 3)])
test_eq(beyond(lr, lr.journey(j.id)).attrgot('slug'), ['mamba', 'transformer-block'])
```

`journeys` lists the walks with the newest change first. `drop_journey`
removes one walk.

``` python
j2 = lr.put_journey(dict(id='sanskrit', title='Read the Gita', goal='read', steps=[]))
test_eq(lr.journeys().attrgot('id'), ['sanskrit', j.id])
lr.drop_journey('sanskrit')
test_eq(len(lr.journeys()), 1)
```

## Tests for walks

A walk from a source has `mode='walk'`. These tests use the small paper
in `tests/walk_data.py` and a fake model.

A walk from a source has one step for each idea of the paper, in the
order of the paper. Each step has the passage to read and a check.

``` python
wl = temp_learning(); did = add_paper(wl)
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
wj = journey_from_source(wl, ask, did)
assert wj.mode == 'walk' and wj.source == dict(shelf='store', doc_id=did, title='Attention Is All You Need') and wj.started is None
assert [s['slug'] for s in wj.steps] == ['sequential-computation', 'softmax', 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk']
r = wj.steps[1]['read']
assert (r['section'], r['page'], r['figure']) == ('3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', 4, 'attention/images/fig2.png')
assert wj.steps[1]['check']['kind'] in ('notebook', 'short') and wj.steps[2]['check']['way'] in ('demo', 'maths')
assert walk_state(wj).total == 3
```

[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state)
gives each step a dot for the rail. `walk_step` keeps a change on one
step.

``` python
ws = walk_state(wl.walk_step(wj.id, 0, done=dict(outcome='fragile', aid='a1', at=1.)))
assert [s.dot for s in ws.steps] == ['shaky', 'now', 'todo'] and ws.current == 1
assert ws.sections == [('1 Introduction', [0]), ('3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', [1, 2])]
assert minutes(wj.steps[1]) >= 2
test_fail(lambda: wl.walk_step('none', 0), contains='none', exc=KeyError)
test_fail(lambda: wl.walk_step(wj.id, 9), exc=IndexError)
```

`merge_journey` changes only the fields that it names. The steps stay as
they are, and an unknown walk raises `KeyError`.

``` python
before = wl.journey(wj.id).steps
test_eq(wl.merge_journey(wj.id, sitting='s1').sitting, 's1')
test_eq(wl.journey(wj.id).steps, before)
test_fail(lambda: wl.merge_journey('none', sitting='s1'), contains='none', exc=KeyError)
```

A concept that you know at depth 4 or more stays in the walk, as known.

``` python
wl.update('softmax', floor=4)
assert journey_from_source(wl, ask, did).steps[1]['status'] == 'known'
```

A walk from pasted text takes the passage only when its quote is in the
text. An idea with no quote in the text has no passage.

``` python
jt = journey_from_text(wl, ask, PAGES[1][1], 'Attention notes')
sm = next(s for s in jt.steps if s['slug'] == 'softmax')
assert jt.source is None and sm['read']['text'].startswith('apply a softmax function')
assert next(s for s in jt.steps if s['slug'] == 'sequential-computation')['read']['text'] == ''
```

A walk from a topic plans the path, then reads from the first passage in
your sources that names each idea. With no sources, a step has no
passage.

``` python
PLAN = dict(title='Attention', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Softmax', statement='', slug='softmax', why='Weights.', needs=[], ways=['code'])])
class Notes:
    name = 'notes'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return [passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My notes', 'Softmax turns scores into weights.')]
jw = walk_from_topic(wl, Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}), 'learn attention', sources=[Notes()])
assert jw.mode == 'walk' and jw.steps[0]['read']['text'].startswith('Softmax turns') and jw.steps[0]['check']
assert walk_from_topic(wl, Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}), 'learn attention', sources=[]).steps[0]['read'] is None
```

A walk across two pages has one step for each idea, in page order.
Softmax is named in both pages. Its step is in the page where its
passage is.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
a = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], 'Introduction', source='https://example.dev/docs/intro', kind='web')
b = lr.vault.add([(0, PAGES[1][1]), (1, PAGES[2][1])], 'Attention', source='https://example.dev/docs/attention', kind='web')
docs = [AttrDict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id'], title=t, url=u) for d, t, u in
        [(a, 'Introduction', 'https://example.dev/docs/intro'), (b, 'Attention', 'https://example.dev/docs/attention')]]
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
j = journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, 'Attention docs')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in j.steps], ['sequential-computation', 'softmax', 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk'])
test_eq([s['read']['doc_id'] for s in j.steps], [a['doc_id'], b['doc_id'], b['doc_id']])   # softmax is named in both; its step is where its passage is
assert j.steps[1]['read']['text'].startswith('apply a softmax function') and j.source['url'] == 'https://example.dev/docs/intro'
test_eq(journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, 'Tool docs', tool='cli').tool, 'cli')         # extra fields go on the walk
```

`progress` hears of each page before the tutor reads it. Two pages with
no section name stay two sections on the rail. A topic walk with
passages from two documents keeps one section.

``` python
heard = []
journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, progress=lambda k, n: heard.append((k, n)))
test_eq(heard, [(0, 2), (1, 2)])
test_eq(walk_state(dict(source=dict(docs=['a', 'b']), steps=[dict(read=dict(doc_id='a', section='')), dict(read=dict(doc_id='b', section=''))])).sections, [('', [0]), ('', [1])])
test_eq(walk_state(dict(source=None, steps=[dict(read=dict(doc_id='a', section='')), dict(read=dict(doc_id='b', section='Intro'))])).sections, [('', [0, 1])])   # a topic walk: one plan section
```

### The title of a paper

A paper that the PDF reader filed by the end of its link has its arXiv
id as its title.
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
now gives the real title for a new walk.
[`paper_id`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#paper_id)
gives the id of the paper of a walk, for a quiet tag, when the title is
not the id.

`repair_titles` fixes the old walks one time. A walk whose title is only
an arXiv id takes the title of its vault document, when that has a real
one. A mark on the shelf says that it ran, as in `repair_names`. It
makes no network call.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L916"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.repair_titles

``` python
def repair_titles()->list:
```

*One time for each shelf, give each walk whose title is only an arXiv id
the title of its vault document, when that has a real one. Return the
ids that changed.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L901"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### paper_id

``` python
def paper_id(
    j
)->str:
```

*The arXiv id of the paper that walk `j` reads, or an empty string.
Empty too when the title of `j` is that id.*

A walk with an arXiv id for a title takes the title of its document. A
walk with a title of its own stays, and so does a walk whose document
has only the id. The repair runs one time.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
real = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], 'Attention Is All You Need', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', kind='pdf')
bare = lr.vault.add(PAGES[1][1], '1706.03763', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03763', kind='pdf')
def paper_walk(jid, title, d, num):
    u = f'https://arxiv.org/pdf/{num}'
    return lr.put_journey(dict(id=jid, title=title, mode='walk', steps=[], url=u, docs=[dict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id'], title=title, url=u)]))
paper_walk('old', '1706.03762', real, '1706.03762'); paper_walk('mine', 'My title', real, '1706.03762'); paper_walk('bare', '1706.03763', bare, '1706.03763')
before = lr.journey('old').updated
lr.v.forget(first(lr.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/titles']))['id'])   # a vault from before the repair
test_eq(Learning(lr.vault).repair_titles(), [])   # the load did it already
test_eq([lr.journey(i).title for i in ('old', 'mine', 'bare')], ['Attention Is All You Need', 'My title', '1706.03763'])
test_eq(lr.journey('old').docs[0]['title'], 'Attention Is All You Need')
test_eq(lr.journey('old').updated, before)
```

``` python
test_eq([paper_id(lr.journey(i)) for i in ('old', 'bare')], ['1706.03762', ''])   # no tag when the title is the id
test_eq(paper_id(dict(title='A page', url='https://docs.example.dev/')), '')
lr.put_journey({**lr.journey('old'), 'title': '1706.03762'}); test_eq(lr.repair_titles(), []); test_eq(lr.journey('old').title, '1706.03762')   # the mark is set
```

The first repair has no network. For a walk or a document that has only
the id, `repair_paper_titles` asks arXiv for the title, with the same
call as
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
([`arxiv_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#arxiv_title),
which keeps the answer on disk), and a short time limit. The app runs it
one time in the background after it starts, never in a load or a
request.

The mark is set only when each id has a title or has failed for good
(arXiv has no such paper). A failure of the network leaves the mark off,
so the next start tries again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L952"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.retitle_paper

``` python
def retitle_paper(
    jid:str, title_of:NoneType=None
)->str | None:
```

*Give walk `jid`, when its title is only an arXiv id, the title of its
paper from `title_of(id)` (default: arXiv). Return the title, or None. A
network failure raises.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/journey.py#L930"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.repair_paper_titles

``` python
def repair_paper_titles(
    title_of:NoneType=None
)->list:
```

*Give each walk and each PDF in the vault that is titled with only an
arXiv id the title of its paper, from `title_of(id)` (default: arXiv).
Return the ids of the walks that changed. The mark is set only when no
id failed from the network.*

The title comes from `title_of`, here a fake. A failure of the network
keeps the id and leaves the mark off, so the next call tries again. A
paper that arXiv does not have is not asked for again.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
d = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], '1706.03762', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', kind='pdf')
paper_walk('w1', '1706.03762', d, '1706.03762'); paper_walk('w2', 'My title', d, '1706.03762')
asked = []
def down(aid): asked.append(aid); raise OSError('no network')
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(down), [])
test_eq((lr.journey('w1').title, first(lr.vault.t.docs(where='id=?', where_args=[d['doc_id']]))['title']), ('1706.03762', '1706.03762'))   # the id stays
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(lambda aid: 'Attention Is All You Need'), ['w1'])                                                        # it tries again
test_eq((lr.journey('w1').title, lr.journey('w2').title), ('Attention Is All You Need', 'My title'))
test_eq(first(lr.vault.t.docs(where='id=?', where_args=[d['doc_id']]))['title'], 'Attention Is All You Need')
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(down), [])      # the mark is set: no new call
test_eq(asked, ['1706.03762'])
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
d = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], '1706.03762', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', kind='pdf'); paper_walk('w1', '1706.03762', d, '1706.03762')
def none(aid): raise Exception('No paper found')
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(none), []); test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(lambda aid: 'X'), [])   # failed for good: the mark is set
test_eq(lr.journey('w1').title, '1706.03762')
```

The old form of an id (`math/0601001`) works the same. The PDF reader
names such a paper by the last part of the id.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
d = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], '0601001v2.pdf', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601001v2', kind='pdf'); paper_walk('w1', '0601001v2.pdf', d, 'math/0601001v2')
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(lambda aid: 'Old ' + aid), ['w1'])
test_eq((lr.journey('w1').title, first(lr.vault.t.docs(where='id=?', where_args=[d['doc_id']]))['title']), ('Old math/0601001v2', 'Old math/0601001v2'))
test_eq(paper_id(lr.journey('w1')), 'math/0601001v2')
```

A walk made from a vault PDF has no address of its own: its `source`
holds only the shelf and the document. The id comes from the source of
that document, or from a title that is only the id. Both walks below
have a document or a title and no link.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
pdf = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], '1706.03762', source='/tmp/papers/attention.pdf', kind='pdf')
arx = lr.vault.add(PAGES[1][1], '1706.03763', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03763', kind='pdf')
mk_vw = lambda jid, title, d: lr.put_journey(dict(id=jid, title=title, mode='walk', steps=[], source=dict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id'], title=title)))
mk_vw('byname', '1706.03762', pdf); mk_vw('bysource', 'Some PDF name', arx); mk_vw('mine', 'My title', pdf)
test_eq([_arxiv_of(lr.journey(i), lr) for i in ('byname', 'bysource', 'mine')], ['1706.03762', '1706.03763', ''])
test_eq(_arxiv_of(lr.journey('bysource')), '')   # without the vault: no address
test_eq(lr.repair_paper_titles(lambda aid: 'Paper ' + aid), ['byname'])   # a walk titled with the id; 'bysource' has a title of its own
test_eq([lr.journey(i).title for i in ('byname', 'bysource', 'mine')], ['Paper 1706.03762', 'Some PDF name', 'My title'])
test_eq(lr.journey('byname').source['title'], 'Paper 1706.03762')
test_eq(first(lr.vault.t.docs(where='id=?', where_args=[pdf['doc_id']]))['title'], 'Paper 1706.03762')
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
pdf = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], '1706.03762', source='/tmp/papers/attention.pdf', kind='pdf'); mk_vw('v', '1706.03762', pdf)
lr.v.add('old', title='old mark', source='learning://marker/paper-titles', kind='marker')   # the first mark does not stop the new repair
def down(aid): raise OSError('no network')
test_fail(lambda: lr.retitle_paper('v', down), contains='no network'); test_eq(lr.journey('v').title, '1706.03762')
test_eq(lr.retitle_paper('v', lambda aid: 'Attention Is All You Need'), 'Attention Is All You Need')
test_eq((lr.journey('v').title, lr.retitle_paper('v', down), lr.retitle_paper('none', down)), ('Attention Is All You Need', None, None))   # a real title: no call
```

A walk has at most `val('walks.steps')` steps. A source with 30 ideas
gives a walk of 12 steps. The model gives 14 numbers, so only its first
12 count. The steps keep the order of the source, but idea 9 needs idea
20, so idea 20 comes first. The other ideas stay on the shelf, and the
walk keeps their slugs in `more`.

``` python
LONG = ' '.join(f'Sentence number {k} of the long text is here.' for k in range(30))
MANY = dict(concepts=[dict(name=f'Idea {k}', statement=f'Idea {k} is one idea.', prereqs=['Idea 20'] if k == 9 else [],
                           quote=f'Sentence number {k} of the long text', ways=['words']) for k in range(30)])
PICK = [21, 1, 4, 10, 6, 13, 16, 19, 23, 25, 28, 30, 2, 3]   # numbers from 1
ml = temp_learning()
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': MANY, 'Return JSON: {"pick"': dict(pick=PICK), 'You write a short note': 'A note.'})
mj = journey_from_text(ml, ask, LONG, 'Long notes')
test_eq(val('walks.steps'), 12)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in mj.steps], [f'idea-{k}' for k in (0, 3, 5, 20, 9, 12, 15, 18, 22, 24, 27, 29)])
assert len(mj.more) == 18 and all(ml.concept(s) for s in mj.more)
```

The build makes two model calls: one finds the ideas and one picks them.
Then a note is written for each of the 12 steps only.

``` python
test_eq(len(ask.calls), 2)
for i in range(len(mj.steps)): tutor_note(ml, ask, mj, i)
notes = [p for p, _ in ask.calls[2:]]
test_eq(len(notes), 12)
assert not any(f'Idea: Idea {k}\n' in p for p in notes for k in (1, 2, 4))
```

A source with 5 ideas keeps all 5, and the model is not asked to pick. A
reply that is not JSON gives the first 12 ideas. A topic plan with 14
steps keeps its first 12.

``` python
few = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=MANY['concepts'][:5])})
fj = journey_from_text(temp_learning(), few, LONG, 'Short notes')
test_eq(([s['slug'] for s in fj.steps], fj.more, len(few.calls)), ([f'idea-{k}' for k in range(5)], [], 1))
bad = journey_from_text(temp_learning(), Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': MANY, 'Return JSON: {"pick"': 'not JSON'}), LONG, 'Long notes')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in bad.steps], [f'idea-{k}' for k in range(12)])
BIG = dict(title='Many', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name=f'Topic {k}', statement=f'Topic {k} is one idea.', slug='', why='', needs=[], ways=['words']) for k in range(14)])
tj = walk_from_topic(temp_learning(), Fake({'Return JSON: {"title"': BIG}), 'many topics')
test_eq((len(tj.steps), tj.more), (12, ['topic-12', 'topic-13']))
```

`true` in the reply is not a number, so it is not idea 1. A reply with
only 2 numbers keeps those 2 ideas, and the first unpicked ideas in
source order fill the walk to 12 steps.

``` python
pk = lambda pick: [s['slug'] for s in journey_from_text(temp_learning(), Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': MANY, 'Return JSON: {"pick"': dict(pick=pick)}), LONG, 'Long notes').steps]
test_eq(pk([True, *range(2, 14)]), [f'idea-{k}' for k in range(1, 13)])
test_eq(pk([29, 30]), [f'idea-{k}' for k in (*range(10), 28, 29)])
```

The path planner and the pick are registered prompts, `walk.plan` and
`walk.pick`. The code reads the text at each call, so a text that you
save on the Settings page is used on the next walk.

``` python
assert {'walk.plan', 'walk.pick'} <= set(PROMPTS)
set_prompt('walk.pick', 'Pick the main ideas. My text.'); set_prompt('walk.plan', 'Plan the path. My text.')
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': MANY, 'Return JSON: {"pick"': dict(pick=PICK), 'Return JSON: {"title"': BIG})
journey_from_text(temp_learning(), ask, LONG, 'Long notes'); walk_from_topic(temp_learning(), ask, 'many topics')
assert {'Pick the main ideas. My text.', 'Plan the path. My text.'} <= {sp for _, sp in ask.calls}
set_prompt('walk.pick'); set_prompt('walk.plan')
```

At most a third of the steps of a walk get a hands-on check
(`walks.hands`). A walk of 12 ideas that all list `code` gets 4 code
checks, on its first 4 steps. The other 8 steps get a short answer in
their text way.

``` python
test_eq([hands_most(n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 12)], [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 4])
CODE = dict(concepts=[{**c, 'ways': ['code', 'words']} for c in MANY['concepts'][:12]])
hj = journey_from_text(temp_learning(), Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': CODE}), LONG, 'Code notes')
test_eq([s['check']['kind'] for s in hj.steps], ['notebook'] * 4 + ['short'] * 8)
assert all(s['check']['way'] == 'words' for s in hj.steps[4:])
```

A walk from a topic has the same cap. Here the plan has 12 topics with a
code way. The first 4 get a code check, and the others get a check in
words.

``` python
CODE_PLAN = dict(title='Code', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name=f'Code topic {k}', statement=f'Code topic {k} is one idea.', slug='', why='', needs=[], ways=['code', 'words']) for k in range(12)])
cj = walk_from_topic(temp_learning(), Fake({'Return JSON: {"title"': CODE_PLAN}), 'code topics')
test_eq([s['check']['kind'] for s in cj.steps], ['notebook'] * 4 + ['short'] * 8)
assert all(s['check']['way'] == 'words' for s in cj.steps[4:])
```

### A walk to a goal from the named sources

The goal names `course22p2`, and the Start box filed it as a chip. The
vault has three of its notebooks on the `notebooks` shelf.

``` python
from abhyasa.ground import passage, VaultSource
```

``` python
GOAL = 'fine-tune my own diffusion model to make a Ramayana comic from the vedicreader episodes'
gl = temp_learning()
NBS = [('nbs/15_DDPM', '# Denoising diffusion\n\nIn this notebook we train a model on images.\n\nWe add noise to each image step by step. The noise schedule sets how much noise we add at each step t.'),
       ('nbs/17_DDPM_v2', '# DDPM, the second version\n\nA cleaner training loop for the same model, with callbacks for each part of the work.'),
       ('nbs/26_diffusion_unet', '# A diffusion U-net\n\nThe U-net takes a noisy image and the step t, and it predicts the noise in the image.')]
for t, x in NBS: gl.vault.shelf('notebooks').add(x, title=t, source=f'/tmp/course22p2/{t}.ipynb', kind='notebook', meta=dict(root='course22p2'))
```

The source map has the root of the chip and each document with its short
title and its first heading. A chip that is not in the vault gives
nothing.

``` python
sm = source_map(gl, ['vault:course22p2', 'vault:nothing', 'link:https://example.com'])
test_eq(sm, [('course22p2', [('15_DDPM', 'Denoising diffusion'), ('17_DDPM_v2', 'DDPM, the second version'), ('26_diffusion_unet', 'A diffusion U-net')])])
test_eq(len(source_map(gl, ['vault:course22p2'], most=2)[0][1]), 2)
```

For a notebook file, the heading comes from its markdown cells, so a `#`
comment in a code cell is not a heading.

``` python
import tempfile
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
```

``` python
nbp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'01_intro.ipynb'
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# check the internet\nimport os'), mk_cell('[[chapter_intro]]\n\n# Your Deep Learning Journey', 'markdown')]), nbp)
test_eq(_nb_heading(nbp), 'Your Deep Learning Journey')
```

The plan prompt has the map and the data list, each in one `<source>`
marker. The planner rules ask for a top-down order.

``` python
pp = plan_prompt(GOAL, srcmap=sm, data=[dict(name='EPISODES', what='the Ramayana episodes')])
assert '<source title="course22p2">- 15_DDPM: Denoising diffusion' in pp and '<source title="data">- EPISODES: the Ramayana episodes</source>' in pp
assert '"doc": str, "hands": str, "makes": str, "data": [str]' in pp
assert 'as fastbook chapter 1 does' in PLAN_SP and 'Stable Diffusion 1.5-class model' in PLAN_SP
```

A fake planner names `15_DDPM` for the first step, and marks the second
step as a notebook that makes `captions.jsonl`. The first step reads its
paragraph from that notebook. The second step keeps its notebook check,
also after
[`cap_hands`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#cap_hands).

``` python
fake = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(steps=[dict(name='Noise schedule', doc='15_DDPM', hands='', makes='', data=[]),
                                                    dict(name='Captions from the episodes', statement='Write one caption for each episode.', doc='', hands='notebook', makes='captions.jsonl', data=['EPISODES'])])})
j = walk_from_topic(gl, fake, GOAL, chips=['vault:course22p2'])
test_eq(j.steps[0]['read']['title'], '15_DDPM'); test_eq(j.steps[1]['check']['kind'], 'notebook'); test_eq(j.steps[1]['makes'], 'captions.jsonl')
test_eq(cap_hands(gl, j.steps)[1]['check']['kind'], 'notebook')
```

The passage is the paragraph with the most main words of the idea, word
for word, with its heading and its shelf. The goal stays on the walk.

``` python
r = j.steps[0]['read']
test_eq(r['text'], 'We add noise to each image step by step. The noise schedule sets how much noise we add at each step t.')
test_eq((r['section'], r['shelf'], r['src'], r['root']), ('Denoising diffusion', 'notebooks', 'vault:notebooks', 'course22p2'))
test_eq(j.goal, GOAL); test_eq(j.steps[0]['doc'], '15_DDPM')
test_eq((j.steps[1]['check']['why'], 'doc' in j.steps[1]), ('it builds your goal', False))
```

With no data list, the step keeps no data. With your data folders, the
planner sees them in the data list, the step keeps the entry that it
names, and the walk keeps the folders.

``` python
assert 'data' not in j.steps[1] and 'data' not in j
fake.rules['You plan a learning path']['steps'][1]['data'] = ['RAMAYANA_EPISODES']
mine = [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='The episodes that my scenarios run on.')]
jd = walk_from_topic(gl, fake, GOAL, chips=['vault:course22p2'], data=mine)
test_eq((jd.data, [d['name'] for d in jd.steps[1]['data']]), (mine, ['RAMAYANA_EPISODES']))
assert "The data list: the learner's own data" in fake.calls[-1][0] and '- RAMAYANA_EPISODES: The episodes that my scenarios run on.' in fake.calls[-1][0]
fake.rules['You plan a learning path']['steps'][1]['data'] = ['EPISODES']
```

A `doc` that is not in the map is dropped. A step with no doc and no
source has no passage.

``` python
bad = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(steps=[dict(name='Text conditioning', doc='99_nowhere')])})
jb = walk_from_topic(gl, bad, GOAL, chips=['vault:course22p2'])
assert 'doc' not in jb.steps[0] and jb.steps[0]['read'] is None
```

[`hands_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#hands_count)
gives the hands-on checks, the steps that are not skipped, and the
notebooks that build the goal. A notebook that builds the goal is not a
hands-on check. Another notebook, such as one for the code way, is. A
skipped step does not count.

``` python
steps = [dict(check=dict(kind='code')), dict(check=dict(kind='short')), dict(check=dict(kind='notebook'), hands='notebook'),
         dict(check=dict(kind='demo'), status='skip')]
test_eq(hands_count(steps), (1, 3, 1))
test_eq(hands_count(j.steps), (0, 2, 1))
```

With no doc, a step reads from the sources. A passage that names the
idea passes. A passage that names only some of its words does not: a
weak match looks like a source, but it is not one.

``` python
class Course:
    name = 'course'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return [passage('vault:notebooks', 'c1', '15_DDPM', 'The noise schedule sets the noise at each step.')]
test_eq(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='n', name='Noise schedule'), [Course()])['ref'], 'c1')
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='n', name='Noise schedule step'), [Course()]), None)   # three words of the name, but not the name
```

A source that the goal named can give a passage that names every main
word of the idea, in any order. Here `15_DDPM` of `course22p2` names
*noise* and *step*. A README in `course22` names only *run* and
*stable*, so the idea “Run Stable Diffusion 1.5 on your Mac” gets no
passage.

``` python
gl.vault.shelf('notebooks').add('Run training on a pool of local GPUs. The stable releases are on PyPI, and each one has its notes.', title='pytorch-image-models/README',
                               source='/tmp/course22/pytorch-image-models/README.md', kind='md', meta=dict(root='course22'))
vsrc = [VaultSource(gl)]
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='s', name='Run Stable Diffusion 1.5 on your Mac'), vsrc, gl, roots=['course22', 'course22p2']), None)
assert _topic_read(AttrDict(slug='t', name='Noise at step t'), vsrc, gl, roots=['course22p2'])['title'] in ('nbs/15_DDPM', 'nbs/26_diffusion_unet')
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='t', name='Noise at step t'), vsrc, gl), None)   # not from a named source: the name must be in the text
```

A doc that the planner names, with no paragraph that names a main word
of the idea, is no source either.

``` python
ddpm = dict(shelf='notebooks', doc_id=gl.vault.shelf('notebooks').doc('nbs/15_DDPM')['id'])
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='l', name='LoRA adapters'), [], gl, ddpm), None)
```

A code block cut in two chunks is still code, so its lines are not a
passage. A passage from a search that is code is not used either.

``` python
test_eq([t for _, t in _paras('```python\ndef f(x):\n    return x\n\ntrain(f, epochs=1, accum=4, finetune=False) report_gpu()\n```\n\nThe loop calls the function on each batch, and it keeps the loss of each step.')],
        ['The loop calls the function on each batch, and it keeps the loss of each step.'])
class Code:
    name = 'code'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return [passage('vault:notebooks', 'k1', '04_mnist', '```python\n# gradient descent: predict, loss, gradient, step\n```')]
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='g', name='Gradient descent'), [Code()]), None)
```

A verse source is for its own subjects. For an ML idea, a verse that
names only some words of the idea is not used. For a Sanskrit idea, it
is.

``` python
class Verses:
    name, subjects = 'verses', ('sanskrit',)
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('verses', 'a1', 'Ramayana 2.69', 'But even as his kind friends did playful comic skits, Bharata was not delighted.')])
test_is(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='c', name='Make the Ramayana comic', subject='ml'), [Verses()]), None)
test_eq(_topic_read(AttrDict(slug='c', name='Comic skits', subject='sanskrit'), [Verses()])['ref'], 'a1')
```

Two chips can have a doc with the same short title. The plan names the
root as `root/title`, and the step reads from that root, not from the
first chip.

``` python
gl.vault.shelf('notebooks').add('# Other notes\n\nThese notes say a few words on the noise schedule, from another course on images.', title='nbs/15_DDPM',
                               source='/tmp/other/nbs/15_DDPM.ipynb', kind='notebook', meta=dict(root='other'))
two = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(steps=[dict(name='Noise schedule', doc='course22p2/15_DDPM')])})
jr = walk_from_topic(gl, two, GOAL, chips=['vault:other', 'vault:course22p2'])
test_eq((jr.steps[0]['root'], jr.steps[0]['read']['root']), ('course22p2', 'course22p2'))
test_eq(_pick_doc('15_DDPM', [('other', '15_DDPM'), ('course22p2', '15_DDPM')]), ('other', '15_DDPM'))   # with no root, the first chip
test_eq(_pick_doc('course22p2 · 15_DDPM', [('course22', '15_DDPM'), ('course22p2', '15_DDPM')]), ('course22p2', '15_DDPM'))
```

## Tests for rabbit holes

The paper has a step on the scaling by √dk. It needs softmax, which you
know, and gradients, which you do not know.
[`needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#needs)
lists both.
[`pick_way_down`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#pick_way_down)
picks a primer for gradients, until gradients needs an idea of its own.

``` python
lr = temp_learning(); did = add_paper(lr)
j = journey_from_source(lr, Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY}), did)
lr.put('Derivatives and gradients', 'The slope of a function at a point, one for each input.', 'ml', slug='gradients')
lr.update('scaling-by-the-root-of-dk', prereqs=['softmax', 'gradients']); lr.update('softmax', floor=3)
test_eq([(n.slug, n.ok) for n in needs(lr, 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk')], [('softmax', True), ('gradients', False)])
test_eq(pick_way_down(lr, 'gradients').how, 'primer')          # no prereqs of its own: a primer is enough
lr.put('Slope of a line', '', 'ml', slug='slope'); lr.update('gradients', prereqs=['slope'])
w = pick_way_down(lr, 'gradients')
test_eq((w.how, w.chain), ('walk', ['slope', 'gradients']))     # a short chain: a side walk, deepest first
```

A side walk is a child of the step that opened it. Each attempt in it
links back to that step. Past depth 2, only its own session can open.

``` python
d = detour(lr, Fake({}), 'gradients', dict(walk=j.id, step=2))
test_eq((d.mode, d.parent, d.depth, [s['slug'] for s in d.steps]), ('walk', dict(walk=j.id, step=2, idea=j.steps[2]['slug']), 1, ['slope', 'gradients']))
test_eq(step_meta(d, 0)['from'], f'{j.id}/2')                  # each attempt links to the step that opened it
assert 'from' not in step_meta(j, 0)                            # a walk with no parent has no `from`
test_eq([t.walk for t in trail(lr, d.id)], [j.id, d.id])
d2 = detour(lr, Fake({}), 'slope', dict(walk=d.id, step=0), how='primer')
test_eq((d2.depth, len(d2.steps), d2.steps[0]['check']['depth']), (2, 1, 2))
test_fail(lambda: detour(lr, Fake({}), 'softmax', dict(walk=d2.id, step=0), how='primer'), contains='deep')
test_eq(detour(lr, Fake({}), 'softmax', dict(walk=d2.id, step=0), how='session').depth, 0)   # past the limit: its own session
```

When you come back, the parent step keeps one line on the side walk.
[`look_up`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#look_up)
finds a term by slug or name. A new term becomes a gap of the step.

``` python
lr.walk_step(d.id, 1, done=dict(outcome='solid', aid='a1', at=1.))
p = back_from(lr, d.id); back_from(lr, d.id)
test_eq(p.id, j.id)
test_eq([(x['walk'], x['slug'], x['outcome']) for x in lr.journey(j.id).steps[2]['detours']], [(d.id, 'gradients', 'solid')])   # once
test_eq(look_up(lr, Fake({}), 'gradients').slug, 'gradients')
test_eq(look_up(lr, Fake({}), 'Derivatives and gradients').slug, 'gradients')                  # by name too
g = look_up(lr, Fake({'The idea: vanishing gradients': dict(name='Vanishing gradients', statement='Gradients near 0 stop the weights.')}),
            'vanishing gradients', at=f'{j.id}/2')
assert g.name == 'Vanishing gradients' and g.slug in lr.concept('scaling-by-the-root-of-dk').gaps   # a new term is filed as a gap of the step
```

A parent step that is gone gives `(None, None)`: a step past the end, a
step that is not a number, a walk that is gone, or no parent.

``` python
test_eq(parent_step(lr, dict(parent=dict(walk=j.id, step=2))), (lr.journey(j.id), 2))
for p in (dict(walk=j.id, step=99), dict(walk=j.id, step='2'), dict(walk='gone', step=0), None):
    test_eq(parent_step(lr, dict(parent=p)), (None, None))
test_eq(parent_step(lr, dict(parent=dict(walk=j.id, step=2)), js={}), (None, None))   # with `js`, only those walks count
```

With no chain on the shelf, the side walk is a short topic walk that
ends on the idea. A side walk that you leave before its last check comes
back as skipped.

``` python
TOPIC = dict(title='Softmax basics', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name=n, statement=f'{n} is one step.', slug='', why='', needs=[]) for n in 'ABCDEF'])
tk = Fake({'You plan a learning path': TOPIC}); n = len(lr.journeys())
dt = detour(lr, tk, 'softmax', dict(walk=j.id, step=2))
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in dt.steps], ['a', 'b', 'c', 'softmax'])     # cut to 4 steps, and it ends on the idea
assert 'Softmax: the basics, enough to read Scaling by the root of dk' in tk.calls[0][0] and len(lr.journeys()) == n + 1   # no path stays
test_eq(back_from(lr, dt.id).steps[2]['detours'][-1]['outcome'], 'skipped')
test_eq((back_from(lr, j.id), trail(lr, j.id).attrgot('walk')), (None, [j.id]))   # a walk with no parent
test_eq(look_up(lr, Fake({}), 'eigenvalues'), None)                                   # a new term with no step: nothing to file
```

Leave a side walk early, then finish it and come back again: the one
record now has the outcome of the finish.

``` python
at0 = lr.journey(j.id).steps[2]['detours'][-1]['at']
lr.walk_step(dt.id, 3, done=dict(outcome='fragile', aid='a2', at=2.))
ds = back_from(lr, dt.id).steps[2]['detours']
test_eq([x['outcome'] for x in ds if x['walk'] == dt.id], ['fragile'])          # one record, now with the outcome of the finish
assert ds[-1]['at'] >= at0
lr.walk_step(dt.id, 3, done=dict(outcome='skipped', at=3.))
test_eq(back_from(lr, dt.id).steps[2]['detours'][-1]['outcome'], 'fragile')       # a later skip does not undo what you learned
```

A parent from Leela is a notebook cell, not a walk. Its side walk has
depth 1, and its attempts link to the cell.

``` python
lw = detour(lr, Fake({}), 'gradients', dict(notebook='nb.ipynb', cell='c1'))
test_eq((lw.depth, step_meta(lw, 0)['from']), (1, 'nb.ipynb/c1'))
assert back_from(lr, lw.id) is None
```

## Open in Leela

Code with a library, tools and a code lookup are learned in Leela.
abhyasa keeps only the small stdlib code check. So a walk can be marked
as a tool walk (`tool=True`), and abhyasa shows a link that opens the
walk, a step or a topic in Leela. abhyasa never calls Leela. It makes a
path and a query. The learner’s browser opens the link on the Leela that
runs on the same computer.

`handoff` makes the path and the query. `read_handoff` is the other
side, for Leela. `HANDOFF_CASES` are the cases that both test suites
run. They are in `abhyasa.contract`, which uses only the standard
library, so Leela reads them with no abhyasa web code. This module gives
the same names.

The link also has the vault key `v`: `vault_key` of the vault that
abhyasa uses. Leela compares it with the key of its own vault. When the
keys are not the same, the two apps use different vaults, and Leela
tells you. A link with no `v` (from abhyasa 0.0.12) works as before.

These cases are shared. Leela runs the same list in its contract test.
The last case has a vault key.

``` python
HANDOFF_CASES[-1]
```

Each case makes its path, and the path reads back to the same values. A
bad id, a bad step and an empty call fail with the name of the key.

``` python
for kw, path in HANDOFF_CASES:
    test_eq(handoff(**kw), path)
    test_eq(read_handoff(path.split('?', 1)[1]), dict(walk=kw.get('jid', ''), step=kw.get('i'), topic=kw.get('topic', ''), v=kw.get('v', '')))
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('walk=../x'), contains='walk')
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('walk=a-1&step=-1'), contains='step')
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('topic=' + 'x' * 201), contains='topic')
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('other=1'), contains='nothing to open')
test_fail(lambda: handoff(), contains='nothing to open')
```

The result reads as attributes too, as Leela uses it. A link with no `v`
gives an empty `v`.

``` python
q = read_handoff('walk=a&step=1&v=0a1b2c3d')
test_eq((q.walk, q.step, q.v), ('a', 1, '0a1b2c3d'))
test_eq(read_handoff('walk=a').v, '')
```

A `v` that is not 8 lower-case hex characters is refused, in the link
that abhyasa makes and in the link that Leela reads.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('walk=a&v=xyz'), contains='v is not a vault key')
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('walk=a&v=0A1B2C3D'), contains='v is not')
test_fail(lambda: read_handoff('walk=a&v=0a1b2c3d%0A'), contains='v is not')
test_fail(lambda: handoff('a', v='xyz'), contains='v is not')
```

The vault key has 8 characters. A path with `~` or `..` gives the key of
the file that it names.

``` python
test_eq(len(vault_key('/tmp/x.db')), 8)
test_eq(vault_key('/tmp/sub/../x.db'), vault_key('/tmp/x.db'))
test_eq(vault_key('~/v.db'), vault_key(Path.home()/'v.db'))
assert vault_key('/tmp/x.db') != vault_key('/tmp/y.db')
```

A tool walk has no code check that abhyasa runs. An idea with the code
way gets a notebook check when the code way is picked. The step of an
idea with the code way has `leela`, so the step page can point to Leela.
A walk to read does not change.

``` python
lr = temp_learning(); did = add_paper(lr)
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
j = journey_from_source(lr, ask, did, tool=True)
assert lr.journey(j.id).tool is True and j.id in [x.id for x in lr.journeys()]   # the marker does not change how a walk is kept
assert all(s['check']['kind'] != 'code' for s in j.steps)
test_eq([bool(s.get('leela')) for s in j.steps], [False, True, False])              # softmax has the code way
plain = journey_from_source(lr, ask, did)
assert not plain.tool and 'leela' not in plain.steps[1]                              # a walk to read does not change
```

The other makers take the same marker. A tool walk from text and from
sources has no code check either.

``` python
jt = journey_from_text(lr, ask, PAGES[1][1], 'Attention notes', tool=True)
assert jt.tool and all(s['check']['kind'] != 'code' for s in jt.steps) and [s['slug'] for s in jt.steps if s.get('leela')] == ['softmax']
test_eq(_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['code'])).kind, 'notebook')
test_eq(_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['code']), tool=True).kind, 'notebook')
test_eq(_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['words']), tool=True).kind, 'short')
```

A code way on a step that needs packages is a notebook check too, on any
walk. A step that the plan marks `hands='notebook'` is always one.

``` python
test_eq(_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['code']), needs=['torch']).kind, 'notebook')
nbc = _check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['words']), hands='notebook')
test_eq((nbc.kind, nbc.way, nbc.depth), ('notebook', 'code', 4))
test_eq(minutes(dict(check=nbc)), 10)
```

A process idea gets an order check, even when a text way comes first in
its list. The extract prompt tells the model when to name `order`. A
walk of 3 steps has 1 hands-on check, so the code check of softmax and
the demo of the scaling become short answers. A tool walk has the same
kinds.

``` python
PROC = dict(concepts=[{**EXTRACT_REPLY['concepts'][0], 'ways': ['words', 'order']}, *EXTRACT_REPLY['concepts'][1:]])
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': PROC})
test_eq([s['check']['kind'] for s in journey_from_source(lr, ask, did).steps], ['order', 'short', 'short'])
assert 'a process or a sequence of steps' in ask.calls[0][1]
test_eq([s['check']['kind'] for s in journey_from_source(lr, ask, did, tool=True).steps], ['order', 'short', 'short'])
```
